items.proposed_content: The cited short-sum methods are alternatives, not stages of one combined proof, but each becomes applicable to zeta only through an explicit interface conversion: logarithmic phases to polynomial moments, isotropic bilinear decoupling to an anisotropic linear box, long sums to shift correlations or scale-adapted blocks, and unweighted cancellation back to the weighted Dirichlet polynomial by Abel summation.

items.proposed_content: Smoothing a prime-zero formula changes its analytic affordances: Mellin decay can make zero and prime contributions absolutely summable enough for interchange, integration, and factorization, while Tauberian or partial-summation steps are then required to transfer information to sharper targets or other weights. In the exhibited smoothed error, isolating the first zero pair yields oscillation only after the remaining tail is bounded.

items.proposed_content: Random-matrix characteristic polynomials reproduce selected universal zero statistics, moment factors, and extreme-value corrections but contain no Euler-product arithmetic. The hybrid Euler-Hadamard representation makes that omission explicit by assigning truncated prime information and nearby-zero information to separate factors whose changes with cutoff compensate in their product.
